_doc: Superstore Saga: Act I Story Graph. Synchronous multi-track retail narrative across Front End, Sales Floor, Receiving, and Specialty.

nodes.text: Welcome to the MegaMart family portal, prospective associate! Before we can process your application for Complex #1042, our automated integrity algorithm needs to understand your core workplace instincts. Three quick questions. No wrong answers! Well... technically there are, but let's have fun with it!

choices.text: Begin the pre-employment integrity assessment.

nodes.text: Question 1: You observe a coworker pocketing a $1.29 pack of strawberry chewing gum from an open box on the loading dock. How do you respond?

choices.text: Immediately notify Security Manager Clint and submit an anonymous loss prevention report.
Mind your own business. You didn't see anything; it's a dollar-thirty.
Ask the coworker if you can have a piece too.

nodes.text: Question 2: You wake up at 5:00 AM with a 102-degree fever and severe chills. Your shift starts in 60 minutes. What is the proper procedure?

choices.text: Take three horse-pill decongestants, wrap a scarf around your neck, and report for duty. Teamwork requires sacrifice!
Call the automated attendance hotline, log the absence, and go back to sleep with your phone on silent.
Show up to work, cough loudly near Store Manager Henderson's desk, and wait for him to send you home.

nodes.text: Final question! It is 11:00 PM on a Saturday. Your shift has officially ended, but five pallets of seasonal merchandise remain untouched in the aisle. Overtime is strictly prohibited by corporate budget. What do you do?

choices.text: Offer to clock out on the terminal first, then stay an extra 45 minutes off-the-clock out of company pride!
Clock out at 10:59 PM on the dot, walk briskly past the pallets, and exit the front sliding doors.
Tell the Area Manager that the morning shift promised to finish them.

nodes.text: Wonderful! The algorithm loves your energy! Compatibility rating: 98.4%! Now, Complex #1042 has four critical staffing vacancies. Where does your retail calling lie?

choices.text: Front End Cashier: Fast hands, customer smiles, and 4011 bananas.
Sales Floor Stocker: Box cutters, freight pallets, and cereal towers.
Backroom Unloader: Heavy freight, Crown forklifts, and hydraulic balers.
Specialty Counter: High-margin tech, electronics warranties, and jewelry.

nodes.text: Fresh meat for Front End. Locker 42 is yours. Grab a navy vest, double-check your name badge, and don't make eye contact with Brenda at Locker 41.
THUMP! Stupid corporate latch! Hey! Rookie! When you get to the lanes, don't let anyone with an accordion binder full of expired manufacturer coupons into your line. Send 'em to Lane Two.
Donna! Who took the brass key to register four?! We have seven buggies backed up into the vestibule and opening bells chime in ten minutes!
Sales floor recruit. Locker 42 is yours. Keep your box cutter retracted in the aisles and don't lean on the paper towel towers—they're load-bearing.
Morning huddle in four minutes! Every grocery shelf needs sub-four-minute facing velocity today. The district VP's algorithm is watching every scan!
Don't listen to Todd, man. If you face the soup cans too fast, he just gives you the 50-pound dog food aisle. Pace yourself.
Backroom freight. Bless your lower vertebrae, kid. Locker 42 is yours. Steel-toes mandatory, and never stand directly behind Crown Forklift Three.
Trailer from the regional warehouse is already backing into Bay Two. Pallets look like they were stacked by a hurricane. We've got two hours to clear thirty tons.
Crown Three is warmed up. Just stay on the yellow pedestrian lines and we won't have any incident reports today.
Specialty counter. High-tech, low sanity. Locker 42 is yours. The glass display key ring weighs four pounds; don't lose it or Security Manager Clint will interrogate you for hours.
Welcome to High Margin, associate. Remember: a customer buying a television without a two-year protection warranty is not a customer—they're a missed opportunity.
Bro, if they hesitate on the warranty, just hit 'em with the store credit card pitch. 29.99% APR builds character.
You've got three minutes before Henderson climbs his milk crate in Action Alley. What do you need before we head out?

choices.text: Donna, what are the golden rules for surviving MegaMart?
How long have you been at Store #1042? Those 30+ service pins look legendary.
Time to head to Action Alley for the morning huddle.

nodes.text: Three rules, kid. Rule one: Never run on the sales floor—walking fast looks professional, running makes management think something is on fire. Rule two: Guard working barcode scanners with your life. Rule three: Store Manager Henderson's smile never reaches his eyes. When his left eyebrow twitches, someone's getting transferred to cart-pushing in a sleet storm.

Fifteen years, three corporate takeovers, four district reorganizations. I've seen managers come and go like cheap two-ply paper towels. Keep your head down, do your eight hours, and never volunteer for inventory night.

Good morning, Complex #1042! Look at this energy! Smell that fresh freight! Today is Regional Efficiency Benchmark Day! District VP Vance is monitoring our real-time sales velocity from regional headquarters! Before we open the sliding doors, let's hear the store cheer! GIVE ME AN M!

choices.text: Scream at the top of your lungs: 'E! WOOOO! LET'S GO #1042!'
Mumble quietly while staring at the linoleum floor: 'E...'
Discreetly check your watch and take a sip from your travel mug.

nodes.text: YES! That's what I'm talking about! That is pure, unadulterated #1042 spirit right there! Look at our rookie taking the lead! All right, team—break out to your departments! LET'S MOVE!
I know the coffee hasn't kicked in yet, team, but our customer satisfaction metrics depend on high-frequency positivity! Let's get out there and drive sales!

Associate. A word. Enthusiasm isn't optional at #1042. It's a key performance indicator. When we don't bring 100% to the morning cheer, the customer feels that deficit. Make sure our energy is aligned tomorrow. Understand?
All right team! Marsha, get front registers online! Todd, stage center aisle freight! Mack, drop that dock plate! Julian, fire up the demo screens! Break out to your stations!

choices.text: Report to Front End Register Lane 4 with Marsha.
Report to Center Grocery Aisles with Todd.
Report to Backroom Receiving Bay 2 with Mack.
Report to the Specialty Tech Counter with Julian.

nodes.text: Here's your U-boat cart, rookie. Cereal aisle needs top-stock consolidation before the lunch crowd hits. But keep your ear on the intercom—if the front end backs up, we're on call.

choices.text: Stack cereal boxes double-speed to beat the morning quota.
Pace yourself and watch Kyle slip behind the paper towel wall.

nodes.text: Trailer door's up! Pallet jack is by the hydraulic lift. Watch the broken floor plate near Bay Two. If Marsha calls an all-hands at the registers, drop your jack immediately.

choices.text: Yank freight pallets with maximum torque to keep Mack on schedule.
Check shrink wrap carefully to avoid a 50-pound pet food collapse.

nodes.text: Keys in hand, associate! First shopper of the day is already hovering by the locked camera case. Smile, quote the two-year accidental protection plan, and be ready for front-end backup.

choices.text: Aggressively pitch the two-year comprehensive warranty.
Just unlock the glass case and give the shopper the HDMI cable.

nodes.text: ALL-HANDS REGISTER SURGE! Register 4 is flashing yellow! We have seven buggies backed up into Action Alley and an irate shopper demanding a manager! Grab your scanner and hold the line!
Not bad for your first rush, rookie. You parried that coupon binder like a seasoned pro. Punch out on the fingerprint scanner, grab a lukewarm coffee, and rest up. Shift 2 starts tomorrow.
Orientation shift concluded. First day survival logged in the employee chronicle. You survived Shift 1 of 56 at MegaMart Store #1042.
